Reportedly, Apple is taking a new approach to introducing artificial intelligence features for users in China: training a large language model on its own with assistance from Alibaba.

A Reuters report, citing three informed sources, said this China-exclusive model marks Apple's departure from its previous strategy of relying on third-party models.

Reports indicate that Alibaba provided support for training the model, though both companies declined to comment.

Models such as ChatGPT and Claude are currently unavailable in mainland China, making Apple's local strategy differ from its approach in other major markets.

This development comes after Alibaba confirmed a partnership with Apple in February 2025. Recently, Chinese internet regulators have registered Apple Intelligence for use on iPhones.

Earlier reports indicated that Alibaba's Qwen model and Baidu's technology would be integrated into the localised system.

Reuters notes that it remains unclear how Apple's new model will operate alongside these third-party models. Apple Intelligence is reportedly expected to arrive in the Chinese market in the coming months via an iOS update.

Additionally, Apple's heavily revamped Siri AI features are expected to launch publicly in applicable regions this autumn alongside iOS 27.

The feature will initially support selected English-language versions, while iPhone and iPad availability in the European Union will be delayed. The timeline for the Chinese market remains unconfirmed.
